title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: choose file extensions from a curated list
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned picker, December rollout, continued enforcement of existing policies and save-time restriction on edited policies. Licensing and the replacement control's preview limitations are supported; minor corrections would complete the control route and align the checklist with the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a pre-curated file extension list for the Endpoint DLP file extension condition.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP now includes a pre curated list of file extensions for the file extension condition.

claims.claim: Previously, free-form entry could include unsupported or non-scannable file extensions.
claims.quote: Previously, file extensions were entered as free form text, which could result in unsupported or non-scannable extensions being used.

claims.claim: The roadmap attributes protection gaps and increased endpoint processing overhead to those unsupported entries.
claims.quote: This could lead to gaps in protection and increase processing overhead on endpoints.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the curated list reduces unnecessary endpoint processing.
claims.quote: This helps improve policy reliability and reduces unnecessary processing on endpoints.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: Learn warns that extension blocking can disrupt unallowed applications accessing files such as .dll, .json and .tmp during normal operation.
claims.quote: certain apps might read or temporarily open files, like .dll, .json, .tmp during routine processes such as rendering, caching, or validating content. If you block these extensions, the app might fail to function properly

claims.claim: Unsupported file extension exclusions is a separate Endpoint DLP setting that narrows unsupported-files coverage.
claims.quote: Because this condition can potentially include many unsupported file extensions, refine detection by adding unsupported extensions to exclude.

claims.claim: Learn about Endpoint data loss prevention contains monitored-file lists and an unsupported-file-types list.
claims.quote: Monitored files ... Unsupported File types ... Endpoint DLP does not support monitoring for the following file types: .sys; .lib; .obj; .mui; .drv; .pf; .crdownload; .ini

claims.claim: No tenant UI or automation control is documented to disable the picker or retain free-form entry.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP curated file extension picker disable tenant switch prerequisites licensing meter' and 'Endpoint DLP curated PowerShell'; inspected dlp-configure-endpoint-settings, New-DlpComplianceRule and Set-PolicyConfig; no picker switch.

claims.claim: The cited portal route starts Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Enterprise applications & devices > Create policy > Custom > Custom policy.
claims.quote: Open Data Loss Prevention > Policies. Select Enterprise applications & devices. Select Create policy and select the Custom from the Categories then Custom policy template from Regulations.
claims.fix: The path correctly reaches the policy wizard but stops early. Extend it to 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Enterprise applications & devices > Create policy > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom policy > Admin units > Full directory > Devices > rule > Actions > Audit or restrict activities on devices > Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions', keeping the Document could not be scanned condition in the note. Also note that the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-sharing-set-unsupported-files puts Create policy before Enterprise applications & devices, whereas this row follows its own cited page.

claims.claim: No complete automation call setting Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'New-DlpComplianceRule EndpointDlpRestrictions unsupported file extensions Apply restrictions only unsupported PowerShell' and 'EndpointDlpRestrictions unsupported Setting'; inspected New-DlpComplianceRule and Set-PolicyConfig; no deciding option documented.

claims.claim: The continuation uses Full directory, Devices, Document could not be scanned and Audit or restrict activities on devices to reach the unsupported-extensions option.
claims.quote: When you select the Audit or restrict activities on devices action in the policy configuration Actions, the Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions shows up.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not quantify the reduction in endpoint processing.
claims.quote: This helps improve policy reliability and reduces unnecessary processing on endpoints.
